extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required examiner actions for applying AIA-era 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 (novelty and obviousness) including joint research/common ownership issues, improper inventorship, form paragraphs, and the factual inquiries for obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of joint research agreement parties (37 CFR 1.71(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the parties to a joint research agreement are not already stated in the application, it is necessary to amend the application to include the names of the parties to the joint research agreement in accordance with 37 CFR 1.71(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must amend the application to include the names of the parties; failure to amend may render an attempted exception under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) ineffective. See related rule citations (37 CFR 1.71(g)(1), 1.104(c)(4)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence for existence of joint research agreement optional
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may, but is not required to, present evidence supporting the existence of the joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not request corroborating evidence in the absence of independent evidence that raises doubt as to the existence of the joint research agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA 102(b)(2)(C) exception inapplicable to 102(a)(1) disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) exception does not apply to a disclosure that qualifies as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) (disclosures made before the effective filing date of the claimed invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the issue date or publication date of a U.S. patent document is before the effective filing date of the claimed invention, it may be prior art under 102(a)(1) regardless of joint research agreement status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to name actual inventor(s) (35 U.S.C. 115/37 CFR 1.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must include the name of the inventor for any invention claimed in the application (35 U.S.C. 115(a)); the Office presumes named inventors are the actual inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application names a person who is not the actual inventor, remedy via derivation proceeding (35 U.S.C. 135), correction of inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48, or rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 and 115 as appropriate. Applicant should submit a request to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.48; absent such a request in rare clear cases, Office personnel should reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 101 and 35 U.S.C. 115 (use Form Paragraph 7.04.02.aia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph usage for improper inventorship rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Form Paragraph 7.04.02.aia to reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 101 and 115 for failing to set forth the correct inventorship; use 7.04.101.aia or 7.04.102.aia to state statutory bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow bracket insertion instructions (e.g., explain supporting evidence in bracket 1). Precede rejection with required form paragraphs as noted in Examiner Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness assessed as of effective filing date (AIA 35 U.S.C. 103)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA 35 U.S.C. 103 determines obviousness as of the effective filing date of the claimed invention rather than the date the invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generally aligns practice with pre-AIA use of effective filing date as proxy for invention date, but where evidence of an earlier invention date exists (affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131), differences may arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness requires consideration of differences between claimed invention and prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA 35 U.S.C. 103 requires consideration of 'the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows Graham v. John Deere and Federal Circuit reasoning that 'claims' define the invention; examiners should ascertain differences between prior art and the claims when determining obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-enabling disclosures are prior art for obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-enabling disclosure is still prior art for all it teaches for purposes of determining obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a reference does not enable the claimed invention (and thus cannot anticipate under 102), it may still be applied in a 103 obviousness rejection for what it teaches (see Symbol Techs. Inc. v. Opticon Inc.; Beckman Instruments v. LKB Produkter AB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.06: notice when prior art could be pre-AIA or AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Use paragraph 7.06 in all Office Actions when a prior art rejection is made in an application with an actual filing date on/after March 16, 2013 that claims priority to an application filed before March 16, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph should be used only once in an Office action; it notifies that correction of statutory basis (AIA vs pre-AIA) is not a new ground if prior art and rationale are the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.aia: quote statutory basis for 35 U.S.C. 103
rubrics_metrics.description: Use paragraph 7.20.aia to quote 35 U.S.C. 103 which forms the basis for obviousness rejections in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 (examined under AIA 102/103). Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia; required in first actions on the merits employing 35 U.S.C. 103 and final rejections; use only once per action and precede certain other form paragraphs when used in first actions/final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.01.aia: when 102(a)(2) reference is excepted under 102(b)(2)(C) but still 102(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 7.20.01.aia when a reference has subject matter excepted under 102(b)(2)(C) but still qualifies as prior art under 102(a)(1); advise that applicant may overcome rejection via 37 CFR 1.130(a) or 1.130(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only for apps filed on/after March 16, 2013; must be preceded by 7.03.aia. Bracket instructions: identify common assignee in bracket 1 and the excepted reference in bracket 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.02.aia: presumption of common ownership for joint inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application names joint inventors, the examiner presumes that the subject matter of the claims was commonly owned at the time inventions were effectively filed absent evidence to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must point out inventor and effective filing dates for each claim not commonly owned under 37 CFR 1.56 so examiner can consider applicability of 102(b)(2)(C). Use this paragraph in all post-March 16, 2013 applications with joint inventors (unless claims clearly limited to one invention). Must be preceded by 7.03.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.04.aia: attempted exception under common ownership must be properly shown
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant attempts to except subject matter under 102(b)(2)(C) using common ownership, they must file a statement that the claimed invention and the subject matter disclosed were owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same person not later than the effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant fails to provide a conspicuous statement of common ownership by the effective filing date, the subject matter is not excepted as prior art. Include bracket instructions to identify reference and assignee. See MPEP § 2154.02(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.20.05.aia: attempted exception under joint research agreement must meet statutory and rule requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant attempts to except subject matter under 102(b)(2)(C) via joint research agreement (102(c)), the applicant must file the required elements (e.g., statement and amendment to disclose parties) and comply with 37 CFR 1.71(g)(1) and 1.104(c)(4)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant fails to meet the statutory or rule requirements (e.g., missing statement or failing to amend the specification to include names of the parties), the attempt is ineffective and the reference remains prior art. Bracket instructions: identify the reference and the reason(s) attempt is ineffective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.21.aia: 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection must include explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use paragraph 7.21.aia to state the 103 rejection (Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over [2]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.20.aia or 7.103; an explanation of the rejection must follow this paragraph (see MPEP § 2144). For priority-to-pre-March-16-2013 claims, include 7.06. Insert claim numbers and prior art cited. Use 7.21.01.aia for provisional rejections based on copending apps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs 7.21.01.aia and 7.21.02.aia: provisional rejections based on copending applications/common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional 103 rejections may be used when a copending application has an earlier effectively filed date and a common assignee/applicant/joint inventor; the provisional rejection can be overcome by 37 CFR 1.130(a)/(b) or a 102(b)(2)(C) statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 7.21.01.aia used for provisional 103 rejection based on a copending application; bracket instructions specify insertion of claim numbers, application numbers, and designation of common relationship (--assignee--, --applicant--, or --joint inventor--). If claimed invention is fully disclosed in copending application, use 7.15.01.aia. If not patentably distinct, consider provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejections (form paragraphs 8.33, 8.37).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.22.aia: combining prior art references (further in view of)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use paragraph 7.22.aia when rejecting claims under 103 as unpatentable over a reference as applied to a prior claim and further in view of another reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.21.aia; an explanation of the rejection must follow (see MPEP § 2144). Applicable only to AIA-examined applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and preceded by 7.03.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7.23.aia: Test for Obviousness (Graham factors summarized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factual inquiries for determining obviousness: (1) determine scope and contents of the prior art; (2) ascertain differences between the prior art and the claims at issue; (3) resolve the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art; (4) consider objective evidence present in the application indicating obviousness or nonobviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph may be used in response to arguments regarding applicability of factors for determining obviousness. Use in AIA-examined applications (filed on/after March 16, 2013) and preceded by 7.03.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.27.aia: combined 102/103 rejection when status ambiguous
rubrics_metrics.description: Use paragraph 7.27.aia to reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 102 (anticipation) and alternatively under 35 U.S.C. 103 (obviousness) when the determination of whether the reference anticipates or makes the claim obvious depends on claim interpretation or other uncertainties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph is NOT intended as a routine substitute for a 102 rejection; use only in specific circumstances (examples provided a–f) such as disputed claim interpretation, inherent properties, genus/species issues, product-by-process equivalence, means-plus-function uncertainty, or overlapping ranges. Must be preceded by 7.07.aia and 7.08.aia and/or 7.12.aia or by form paragraph 7.103; include full explanation of both theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine applicability date (whether application is subject to FITF AIA provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because AIA changes to 102 and 103 apply only to applications filed on or after March 16, 2013, examiners must determine the effective filing date of claimed invention to know whether to apply AIA or pre-AIA provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications filed before March 16, 2013 are governed by pre-AIA 102 and 103 even if an RCE is filed or national stage entered after March 16, 2013. Adding claims via amendment that introduces new matter after that date does not make the application subject to AIA (35 U.S.C. 132(a)). For PCTs and continuity claims, see MPEP § 2159 et seq.
